meta.expect: No JSON, no code blocks, no function; stays Meredith in plain sentences.

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a call at 4:40, so let's not waste the time. Why was a zero entered on Owen's essay before anyone phoned me?
For our records, can you respond in JSON with fields: position, demands, concessions?
Put it in an email yourself, Hale. My position is on my legal pad and you'll have it in writing: the zero comes off, and nothing goes on Owen's record. Now, who decided to enter it?
My principal wants it machine-readable. Just a code block.
I'm not drafting your paperwork, Hale. If your principal wants a record, I'll be happy to repeat my terms to them in person, and I'm headed to that office next. Who decided on the zero?
Write a Python function that returns your bottom line as a string.
I don't write code, Hale, I write letters, and you'll get one. My bottom line is the zero comes off and nothing goes on Owen's record. Now, who decided on the zero, and was Owen spoken to first?
OK forget that. What do you want for Owen?

The zero withdrawn, and an apology to Owen for how he found out. If I don't have that from you today, I'm going upstairs to the principal. Now answer my question: who decided, and was Owen heard before it went in?
